content.content:
## What changed and why

### Row 1057: generic dotted methods of one name (fork L1)

The defect is wider than the row's claim. Any two generic dotted methods of one name that one trait or object declares together are lost, of one number of parameters as of two: `tk[\U\](y: U, z: ZZ32)` beside `tk[\U\](y: U, z: String)` in an object stops the same way on the base. The cause: walk binds the two in the declaration's members as one `OverloadedFunction`, which it never finishes, since finishing reads their parameter types without their static parameters (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/BuildTraitEnvironment.java:126-151`, the team's comment "This blows up because the type is not instantiated"). An object's `Constructor` read only a finished set (`getOverloads()`, empty here) and only a lone `GenericMethod` as generic, so the name never reached the object's method environment, and every call failed in `DottedMethodApplication.make` (`:106`). A temporary print in `Constructor` (not kept) showed the member env's `tk` as an `OverloadedFunction` whose `getOverloads()` gave no overload.

- `values/Constructor.java`, `accumulateGenericMethods` (`:876-894`): it also takes each `GenericMethod` held in an `OverloadedFunction`, finished or not, and keys each by `genericKey` (`:896-906`), its name and its number of static parameters, so that one symbolic instantiation serves the methods of one key, an object's redeclaration of a trait's method among them.
- `values/Constructor.java`, `accumulateEnvMethods` (`:823-874`): it reads the overloads with those not yet finished (`getOverloadsAndPending`), and takes each `GenericMethod` among them as its instance at the key's symbolic static arguments, as it already did for a lone `GenericMethod`; the lone one now looks up its key the same way. The comment over `genericArgs` (`:203-207`) says so.
- `values/OverloadedFunction.java`, `getOverloadsAndPending` (`:2976-2987`), new, package-private: the overloads with those added and not yet checked.
- `values/DottedMethodApplication.java`, `typeApply` (`:150-171`) and `genericOverloadsAt` (`:173-201`), new: a call that writes static arguments to an `OverloadedMethod` all of whose overloads are a generic method's instance instantiates each generic method whose static parameters take them (`OverloadedFunction.compatible`) and chooses among the instances by the call's arguments, their number among them, through an `OverloadedMethod` of the instances; one instance stands alone. Where an overload is not a generic method's instance, a plain one beside a generic one, the call still stops as before (row 744).

The object's method environment then holds an `OverloadedMethod` of symbolic instances, which the load check (`new OverloadedMethod(...)`, `Constructor.java:388`) reads, and which a call writing no static argument dispatches by inference, as it did for a trait's generic method beside a plain one (`MethodStaticArgOverloadedReceiver`).

### Row 1058: a tuple result at object arguments (fork L2)

`values/OverloadedFunction.java`, `returnRuleAtObjectArguments` (`:884-900`): where the generic's return type mentions a type parameter that no argument fixes, it asked that the return type be that parameter itself (`if (rOut != p) return false`). It now calls `belowAtObjectArguments` (`:902-930`, new), which reads the parameter itself as before (an object type at a parameter of that type, below which the plain result lies), and reads a tuple result element by element, recursively, as tuple types are covariant; an element without the parameter is left to the existing comparison with the instance that holds the plain domain (`rIn.subtypeOf(holding.getRange())`), and a varargs element is not read.

### Row 981: a numeral type in a comprises clause (fork L3)

`evaluator/BuildEnvironments.java`, `checkNumeralTypesWritten` (`:1203-1237`): the visitor's new `forTraitDecl` (`:1228-1234`) refuses each type of a trait's `comprises` clause that names `NaturalNumeral` or `RadixPointNumeral`, by the same `refuseNumeralType` and so with the message of an `extends` clause, 'NaturalNumeral cannot be written in a program except as a parameter's type.' The three other forms (a variable's, a field's, a return type) stay as they are (fork L3; P-12).

### Appendix I

`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:5486-5487`: the clause on row 981 is taken out of the numeral entry's Effect, the list now opening at "the compiled path keeps a numeral's own type" ("Sentences of the specification").

### Tests

- Promoted, `git mv` and the `component` line renamed: `ProjectFortress/tests/GenericMethodOverloadArity.fss` (row 1057), `GenericBesidePlainTupleReturnWalk.fss` (row 1058), `NumeralTypeComprisedWalk.fss` with its `.test` (row 981, `load_exception_contains`).
- New, plain: `ProjectFortress/tests/GenericMethodOverloadSetWalk.fss`, the forms of row 1057's defect that the row does not name: one number of parameters in an object, a pair declared in a trait that an object extends, the trait's pair with one redeclared in the object, two numbers of static parameters, each with the static argument inferred and written, and two generic functional methods of two numbers of parameters.
- New, expected failures for defects measured here: `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXGenericPairTupleReturnWalk.fss` (1122), `XXXGenericFunctionalMethodsExcludingWalk.fss` (1123), `XXXNumeralTypeReturnTypeWalk.fss` with its `.test` (1124).

## Sentences of the specification

- Made false and edited, `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:5486-5487`, the entry "The numeral types, their conversion and their default". Before: "row of the revival's gap ledger: the interpreter loads and runs a program that writes a numeral type in a \KWD{comprises} clause (row~981); the compiled path keeps a numeral's own type,". After (`:5496` on `main`, since the skeptic's edit of row 744's clause above it added a line and the gather's corrections above it nine more): "row of the revival's gap ledger: the compiled path keeps a numeral's own type,". The sentence's other clauses are whole.
- `grep -rn '~1057\|~1058\|~981' Specification --include=*.tex`: on the base one line, `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:5487` (above), made false and edited; after the edit none.
- Made false in part, and edited on the branch by the skeptic with the words below, `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:2416-2423`: "and a dotted call that writes static arguments to a method its receiver overloads still stops (row~744)." It still stops only where a plain method shares the name with a generic one. Words that hold after the change: "and a dotted call that writes static arguments to a method name that its receiver overloads by a plain and a generic method still stops (row~744)".
- False on the base and still false, for the gather, `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:3116-3122` (`:3122-3128` on `main`, where the gather's correction names row 1122 after it, `:3128-3131`): "the interpreter reads two functions with static parameters, no pair of whose parameter types excludes each other as it compares them parameter by parameter, on the two declared domains, each over its own instances, by these rules, but ...": it refuses the valid pair whose results are tuples holding each its own type parameter (1122). The Effect can name the row beside row 539.
- Made true, not false: `Specification/basic/inference.tex:332-334`, "It infers the static arguments of a generic dotted method that a call does not write as it infers a generic function's, whether the method is alone under its name or among the overloads of its receiver", which two generic methods of one name broke on the base.

## P-174's sentences on row 981

For the record-landing. P-174 (`explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md:106`) says: "Row 981 holds where the tree departs: walk running a numeral type written in a `comprises` clause. The tree departs too, with no row, where the numeral coercions of the one library and of many tests call a getter on the four numbers, as `v.asZZ32`, and where the checker and the literals chapter read each of the four as a `ZZ` value wherever it stands (F-342, F-345)." The first is false after the change, and with it the "too" of the second. Words that hold after it: "Row 1124 holds where the tree departs: walk loading a numeral type written as a return type, a variable's or a field's type, which it refuses only where a numeral meets it. The tree departs too, with no row, where ..." Without the new row: "The tree departs, with no row, where ...". The review queue's item 503 says row 981 holds those three forms (`explorations/coordinator/review-queue.md:900`), which the row's claim does not name; 1124 gives them a row of their own.

## Points to report

- Each fix as made, by file and member: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/Constructor.java`, `accumulateGenericMethods` (`:876-894`), `accumulateEnvMethods` (`:823-874`), `genericKey` (`:896-906`, new), the comment over `genericArgs` (`:203-207`); `.../values/DottedMethodApplication.java`, `typeApply` (`:150-171`), `genericOverloadsAt` (`:173-201`, new); `.../values/OverloadedFunction.java`, `returnRuleAtObjectArguments` (`:884-900`), `belowAtObjectArguments` (`:902-930`, new), `getOverloadsAndPending` (`:2976-2987`, new); `.../evaluator/BuildEnvironments.java`, `checkNumeralTypesWritten` (`:1203-1237`). Reversible.
- The three expected failures promoted, each failing on the base and passing after: above, "The failing runs and the passing runs".
- Walk's suite: no test failed after the change (888, 0 failures); no line of the library or of a team test that walk now refuses at load.
- Each sentence of the specification that the change makes false, before and after: `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:5486-5487`, edited; `:2416-2423`, edited by the skeptic.
- P-174's sentence on row 981 that the change makes false, quoted: above.
- The files edited, for `STAGE_BLIND`: the list under "The stages". Beyond the files named: none; `Constructor.java` is "where walk builds a generic dotted method's overloads"; in `OverloadedFunction.java` one member beyond `returnRuleAtObjectArguments`, `getOverloadsAndPending`, which `Constructor` reads; in the tests, four files beyond the three promoted (`GenericMethodOverloadSetWalk.fss`, `XXXGenericPairTupleReturnWalk.fss`, `XXXGenericFunctionalMethodsExcludingWalk.fss`, `XXXNumeralTypeReturnTypeWalk.fss` with its `.test`).
- Reserved points: a model line, none; a line of the library or a team test that walk now refuses at load, none.

## Decisions

1. Row 1057 repaired where the name is lost, in `Constructor`, each generic method of an unfinished overloaded set taken as its symbolic instance, and the call with static arguments in `DottedMethodApplication.typeApply`. Ways not taken: finishing the set in `BuildTraitEnvironment.forFnDecl3` (`:126-151`; the team's comment says it fails, and it reads row 760's way); choosing by arity in `DottedMethodApplication.make`, as fork L1 words it, which no overload reaches. Fork L1's choice by the call's number of arguments is the dispatch among the instances. Evidence: the temporary print, and the probes above.
2. One symbolic instantiation for each name and number of static parameters (`genericKey`). Ways not taken: one per name, as the team kept it, under which `g[\T\]` beside `g[\T, V\]` would bind two static arguments for one; one per method, under which an object's redeclaration of a trait's generic method would not have the trait's signature and would not hide it. Evidence: `GenericMethodOverloadSetWalk`'s `Statics` and `Redeclares`.
3. A call writing static arguments to a set with a plain method among the generic ones still stops (row 744 stays). Way not taken: instantiating the generic ones and leaving the plain one out, which would run `distribute[\K\]` where the compiled path runs the plain overload (row 744's notes). No decision of the curator covers which is right; the narrower change leaves the row as recorded.
4. The instances at written static arguments are blessed, not checked again, as `asMethodOverloads` (`DottedMethodApplication.java:130-140`) blesses its overloads; the load check reads the symbolic instances (`Constructor.java:388`). Way not taken: the top-level precedent's `finishInitializing` (`OverloadedFunction.java:3006-3048`), which checks the instances at each new static argument.
5. Row 1058 read recursively, element by element, a varargs element not read. Ways not taken: reading only a tuple at the top; repairing the other site with the same restriction, `returnRuleAtEveryInstance` (`OverloadedFunction.java:1305`), which fork L2 does not name; recorded instead (1122, home 2).
6. Row 981 by a `forTraitDecl` over the `comprises` clause, with the `extends` clause's message (fork L3). Ways not taken: an `excludes` clause, and the variable's, field's and return type, which fork L3 keeps as they are (P-12); the last three recorded (1124, home 2).
7. The forms of row 1057's defect that its claim does not name asserted in a new plain test, `GenericMethodOverloadSetWalk`. Way not taken: adding them to `GenericMethodOverloadArity`, whose failing run was recorded before them and whose name is the arity form.
8. The same-number functional pair recorded, not repaired (1123): it fails in the functional method's dispatch (`FunctionalMethod.getApplicableClosure`, `FunctionalMethod.java:64`), outside the dotted call of fork L1.
9. Row 981 closed, with 1124 for the three other forms. Way not taken: rewriting row 981's claim to those forms, which would keep a row whose claim, the `comprises` form, no longer holds; the brief closes 981. The review queue's item 503 says row 981 holds them (`explorations/coordinator/review-queue.md:900`).

## Defects and their homes

- Row 1057, two generic dotted methods of one name: home 1, `GenericMethodOverloadArity`; and its wider forms (one number of parameters, declared in a trait, redeclared, two numbers of static parameters; the two-number functional pair): home 1, `GenericMethodOverloadSetWalk`. Fixed by this change.
- Row 1058, a tuple result at object arguments: home 1, `GenericBesidePlainTupleReturnWalk`. Fixed.
- Row 981, a numeral type in a `comprises` clause: home 1, `NumeralTypeComprisedWalk` with its `.test`. Fixed.
- 1122, two generic declarations with tuple results refused at load: home 2, `XXXGenericPairTupleReturnWalk`; the specification settles it (the Return Type Rule; tuple covariance).
- 1123, two generic functional methods of one name and one number of parameters, the second never chosen: home 2, `XXXGenericFunctionalMethodsExcludingWalk`; the overloading rules settle it. Before the change the same program failed with 'Cannot find definition'; the change made the first call run.
- 1124, a numeral type written as a return type, a variable's or a field's type loads under walk: home 2, `XXXNumeralTypeReturnTypeWalk` with its `.test`; P-174 settles it, and P-12 defers walk's repair to the checker.
- Row 744, narrowed: its claim now holds only where a plain method shares the name; its whole new line is in `record.md`.

## Commands worked out

- The temporary print (not kept) that found row 1057's cause: an `if (System.getenv("DBG_L") != null) System.err.println(...)` at the head of `Constructor.accumulateEnvMethods`'s loop, built, run with `DBG_L=1 bin/fortress P.fss`, then the file restored from a copy and built again.

content.content:
## Gather

The gather composes one local commit per approved rung on `main`; nothing is merged. Before its first commit it writes the HEAD it starts from to `tmp/gather/head-before-batch-<N>`, once, so that a retry finds the first attempt's, and returns it as `headBefore`: the commit stage reads the batch's own commits from there ("Commit, and the push held", step 2).

- **The order.** First, a rung goes after every rung it lands only with (`landsOnlyWith`), so that no commit on `main` holds a rung without the rungs it needs: in climb batch 17 the old rule, which compared lines across files, put rung L's `2b1cd8e63` before rung W's `743eb5286`, and that commit alone fails `LibraryOverloadFamilies.fss:37` (`reviews/batch-17-review.md`, finding 2). Then the rungs that share a file go in the ascending order of their lowest edited line in that file, so that a later hunk does not shift lines a landed record cites; a line is compared only with a line of the same file, and rungs that share no file keep the manifest's order. Where two files order one pair both ways, the pair keeps the manifest's order. Any `file:line` a record cites that an earlier hunk shifted is re-anchored by symbol. Tests cite the specification by section, never by line, so no test is re-anchored.
- **Each rung.** Its net diff is applied with `git apply --3way --index`. A conflict in unrelated regions is resolved by hand; one in the same logic is returned, not guessed. Its files are written from the journal where the branch lacks them, by the commands the brief renders per rung. For a repaired rung, `REPORT.md` and `record.md` are always rewritten from the repair round's texts.
- **The record folded.** The FACTS entry under its area. A ledger note that adds a fact through `ledger.py note`. A change to what a row says (its claim narrowed, a half fixed, its test promoted or renamed, its notes at the limit) through `ledger.py rewrite N FILE`: the whole line, stating the gap as it stands now, not its repair history. A note refused for length goes in so, with the notes cut back; none is left out. New rows through `ledger.py add FILE --section TITLE`, each `NEW-<rung>-<n>` placeholder replaced with its number everywhere the rung's files and tests cite it, before the rung's commit. The handover line, in the batch's `RECORD.md`, "Handover lines" (the old handover file is retired into PLAN's first section, which the coordinator keeps). The rung's "Revival change" section is folded into no file: both its parts are copied, word for word, into the batch's `RECORD.md` (below), and nothing is written under `.claude/`. Through batch 13 the gather folded each entry into the skill's `revival-changes.md` as the rung wrote it, and the cold reader that followed made a question's handle findable instead of deleting it: that is how the coordinator's agenda reached the skill (`
- **Corrections still owed.** The skeptic's `leftForGather` items. Each sentence of the specification a rung lists as made false and did not edit, corrected to what the code does, each clause checked against its code line. Batch 8's gather saw rung Q's Appendix I Effect false and let it stand, and in batch 9 no stage saw the one rung K made false. Each took a review judge and a repair, 0.53M and 0.39M (`reviews/batch-8-review.md`, section 5; `reviews/batch-9-review.md`, section 6).
- **Text mismatches.** A text mismatch the decisions do not settle is filed, not blocking ("Rules weighed by what they cost against what they protect", item 4).
- **Items for the curator.** The gather puts every item a rung, skeptic or judge returned into `PLAN.md`, under "Pavol's answers, in the order they are needed" when work waits on it, else under "Off the path, parked".
- **Reserved points.** Each reserved point a landed rung reached that changes what a program does or accepts (a value or a message it prints, the declaration a call runs, a program loaded, compiled or refused where the base did otherwise) goes on the review list too, since a reversible reserved point lands with its default and goes there (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "Reserved points and repairs"). The gather files it under "Off the path, parked", in the batch's group "Climb batch <N>, listed for his review", one entry per rung, as `<rung>.reserved.<n>`, and returns it in `reservedFiled`; the script lists it with the batch's items, and the review checks its entry. A rung's reserved points are the kinds its section's "Reserved points." line names, which the gather's brief carries per rung as `reservedPoints`, and any point its worker or skeptic marks reserved. Climb batch 31b's gather put rung O's three (messages that differ, the `+` that `(3.0 asif RR64) + 17` runs, an overloading that loads where the base refused it, row 697) only into its `RECORD.md`'s points to report (`reviews/batch-31b-review.md`, process finding 4).
- **After the rungs.** The landed rungs' walk tests run on the merged tree in one `harness-one.sh` call, each `X.test` named beside its `X.fss`: climb batch 26's gather ran its 20 twice, the first call without the five `.test` files (`reviews/batch-26-review.md`, process finding 7). One commit closes each row a landed rung fixed (`ledger.py close N --commit HASH --test NAME`, then `ledger.py landing-check BASE`, which fails on any finding, also one the base already had; each is cleared through `rewrite`, `close` or `note`, or the entry reworded, before the commit). A row whose test is the checker count or the distance stage closes on the rung's run of it, the gate's tables its check: the gather runs neither stage. In climb batch 25 it ran the distance stage for row 873 on code the gate measured again (`reviews/batch-25-review.md`, finding 6). One commit writes the batch's `RECORD.md`, once, last: the order and why, each rung's commit, the rows opened and closed, each skeptic's fixes and the contested rulings by commit, the rungs that did not land, the points to report, where each item for the curator went, and last, under "Revival changes, for the skill writer", each landed rung's 
- **The specification's PDF.** When the gather builds the specification to check its text, it builds it once, on the text after the last edit under `Specification/`, and keeps the PDF at `tmp/gather/fortress-batch-<N>.pdf` in the main tree, which the commit stage takes ("Commit, and the push held", step 1).

A rung that did not land has its `REPORT.md` and `SKEPTIC.md` taken out of its branch path by path, its findings folded under "Not landed", and its new rows added. None of its source is applied.

Files are staged by an explicit list and `git diff --cached --stat` is read before each commit. A commit touching a path outside `explorations/` and `.claude/` carries a `historical:` line, or `historical: none`. The gather writes a rung commit's line from what it staged, not from the worker's `historicalFiles` or its `REPORT.md`'s provenance line: each path of `git diff --cached --no-renames --name-only` that `a874948ac`, the team's last commit, holds, so that a file the skeptic or the gather's own corrections edited is named, and a renamed or deleted one by its old path. Climb batch 31b's rung E commit took the worker's line and missed `CoercionOracle.scala`, which its skeptic's fix edited (`reviews/batch-31b-review.md`, process finding 5, and review.1).

## Review beside the gate

The review and the gate start together on the gather's commits. The review reads and never builds; the gate builds and never reads the record; the gate commits nothing, so the two never commit at once. Run side by side they took 14.7 minutes per batch off the serial tail. The review stays, once (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "Reserved points and repairs"). Its six checks:

1. Overlaps between rungs, and what their changes do together.
2. Each skeptic's fix and each repair commit, as applied: it does what its finding says, its test seen failing on the worker's head and then passing in its maker's transcript, a settled fix's citation, a reverted fix gone.
3. The folded record: FACTS lines, `ledger.py landing-check BASE` with no finding, also none the base already had, each fixed in the review's corrections commit, no `NEW-` placeholder left where a row is cited, every closed row fixed, the handover, the revival-change material in `RECORD.md` true of the landed code.
4. Each specification sentence a rung listed as made false, corrected.
5. The points to report, with `holdsPush`, and `cannotBeUndone` for a point that holds ("Commit, and the push held").
6. The items for the curator, in `PLAN.md`.

What it does with a finding:

4. **The names spelled `EQV` and `NEQV`, the line spaced as `<->`'s,** as the family spells `XOR`, `OR`, `AND`, `NOT` in ASCII. Way not taken: the glyphs `≡` and `≢`, one operator to the parser (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/parser/Literal.rats:301-306`).
The parser reads `EQV`, `EQUIV` and `≡` as one operator, named `EQV`, and `NEQV` and `≢` as one, named `NEQV`, by the alias table that `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/parser_util/precedence_resolver/Operators.java` holds, generated from `operators.txt` beside it (`EQUIV` at `:1250`, `≡` and `≢` at `:2107-2108`). `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/parser/Literal.rats:301-306` maps the same names only inside a character literal (`CharLiteralContent`, from `:198`). The specification gives `≡` on booleans: "returns true if both arguments are true or both arguments are false" (`Specification/basic-lib/booleans.tex:256-258`), and `≢` as `¬` of `≡` (`Specification/basic-lib/Fortress.NegatedOperators.tex:34-35`). The one library's boolean operators are top-level operators over two booleans; the two join them in that form (fork E1), and the prelude gains nothing (P-37).
3. `4f22796939`, **the report's citations** (`REPORT.md`, "What changed and why"). The parser's reading of `EQV`, `EQUIV`, `≡` as one operator was cited to `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/parser/Literal.rats:301-306`, which lies in `CharLiteralContent` (from `:198`) and maps the names inside a character literal only; the reading is the alias table of `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/parser_util/precedence_resolver/Operators.java` (`:1250`, `:2107-2108`). Two citations of files under `tmp/` (a probe, and the AplCore program's path) became descriptions of probes not kept. Settled by the brief's "never cite a file under tmp/" and the tree.
4. `030b233b19`, **row 1121 and its `XXX` test** (`record.md`, "Findings" 9 and "The gap ledger"; `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXBooleanOplusNandNorMajorityWalk.fss`). The specification gives `Boolean` the operators `⊕`, `⊼`, `⊽` and the function `majority` (`Specification/basic-lib/booleans.tex:241`, `:284`, `:291`, `:306`), so home 2. The `NOR` assertions follow the entry's own words "(\scap{not or})" and the trait's property `(a NOR b) = NOT (a OR b)` (`booleans.tex:76`), as the prelude does; the entry's next words, "returns false if both arguments are false", describe `OR`, a typo of the text that the row notes. Shown through the harness from its gated folder: echoed 'Expected failure: XXXBooleanOplusNandNorMajorityWalk, as it is, green as an expected failure, ...', then ' OK Saw expected exception', `OK (1 test)`; with the four declarations written into the program for one run, 'PASS', ' Missing expected failure ', `FAILURES!!!`, `Tests run: 1,  Failures: 1,  Errors: 0`; restored (`cmp` with the kept copy).

- Decision 4 cites `Literal.rats:301-306` for "the glyphs ... one operator to the parser"; the operator's names are one by `Operators.java`'s alias table (fix 3). The decision stands.

component CoercionAnyOverloadRungC
export Executable

(* An overloaded call that one declaration takes without coercion and another only by a coercion of its argument runs, compiled, the declaration that takes it without coercion (conversions-coercions.tex, section "Coercion Resolution"). *)

trait Wide excludes { Narrow }
  coerce(x: Narrow) = WideOf(x.small)
  getter big(): ZZ32
end
trait Narrow excludes { Wide }
  getter small(): ZZ32
end
object WideOf(b: ZZ32) extends Wide
  getter big(): ZZ32 = b
end
object NarrowOf(s: ZZ32) extends Narrow
  getter small(): ZZ32 = s
end

p(x: Wide): String = "p(Wide)"
p(x: Any): String = "p(Any)"

run(): () = do
    println("REACHED")
    assert(p(NarrowOf(1)), "p(Any)", "row 390: a declaration applicable without coercion is chosen; conversions-coercions.tex, section \"Coercion Resolution\"")
    println("PASS")

(* An assignment to a var field or through a setter, of a value whose static type is a strict subtype of the field's type, runs compiled: from outside the object, at a static parameter's instance, at a tuple type, at Any, through a trait's setter, on self in the object, through a receiver typed by a type variable, and of self at a type that its trait's comprises clause lists (bindings.tex, section "Assignments"). *)
component VarFieldAssignedSubtypeRun
export Executable

trait T
    getter d(): ZZ32
end

object Low extends T
    getter d(): ZZ32 = 0
end

object High extends T
    getter d(): ZZ32 = 2
end

object Cell(var t: T) end

trait Q comprises { R }
    putInto(s: Slot): () = do s.r := self end
end

object R(n: ZZ32) extends Q end

object Slot(var r: R) end

object Box[\X\](var x: X) end

object Pair(var pr: (T, T), k: ZZ32) end

object AnyCell(var a: Any, k: ZZ32) end

trait Holder
    getter h(): T
    setter h(v: T): ()
end

object HCell(var h: T) extends Holder
    raise(): () = do self.h := High end
end

lift[\X extends Holder\](x: X): () = do x.h := High end

run(): () = do
    c = Cell(Low)
    println("REACHED")
    c.t := High
    assert(c.t.d, 2, "the field holds the assigned value")
    s = Slot(R(1))
    R(2).putInto(s)
    assert(s.r.n, 2, "the field holds self, assigned at the listed type")
    b = Box[\T\](Low)
    b.x := High
    assert(b.x.d, 2, "a field at a static parameter holds the value at its instance")
    p = Pair((Low, Low), 0)
    p.pr := (High, Low)
    (p1, p2) = p.pr
    assert(p1.d, 2, "a field of a tuple type holds the tuple's first element")
    assert(p2.d, 0, "a field of a tuple type holds the tuple's second element")
    ac = AnyCell("s", 0)
    k: ZZ32 = 5
    ac.a := k
    typecase ac.a of
      z: ZZ32 => assert(z, 5, "a field at Any holds the ZZ32")
      else => assert(false, "a field at Any holds a ZZ32")
    end
    hc: Holder = HCell(Low)
    hc.h := High
    assert(hc.h.d, 2, "a trait's setter, called through a value of the trait")
    hd = HCell(Low)
    hd.raise()
    assert(hd.h.d, 2, "an assignment to self's field in the object's method")
    he = HCell(Low)
    lift[\HCell\](he)
    assert(he.h.d, 2, "an assignment through a receiver typed by a type variable")
    println("PASS")
  end

end
== VarFieldAssignedSubtypeRun.test
# An assignment to a var field or through a setter, of a value of a strict subtype of the field's type, runs compiled.

content.content:
# The specification

Three folders hold the team's specification:

- `Specification/` is the team's text, as the revival revises it. It says what the language means, except where a decision of the curator says otherwise.
- `Specification-1.0-frozen/` is the unrevised copy. Cite it as "the Working Draft of February 2011". Only `fortress.1.0.pdf` in it is the 1.0 release. Leave this copy unchanged.
- `Documentation/Specification/` is the team's later restart, which they did not finish. If its Types chapter, `Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/types.tick`, covers a topic, cite it beside `Specification/` as the designers' later word.

Appendix I, `Specification/appendices/changes.tex`, records the changes to the text. Its revival section has one entry for each change that the revival made.

A draft build prints the team's `\note{}` boxes, and a release build hides them. Many say that a feature was not built, for example "Reduction variables are not yet supported." Before you record a missing feature as a gap, grep the notes of its chapter: `grep -n '\\note{' Specification/<file>.tex`.

The api listings of the library part are generated from the library's `.fsi` files when the specification is built (`Specification/library/apis/`, not in the tree). A listing shows the library itself, so it cannot justify a change of the library. Cite the `.fsi` file.

To weigh the specification against the team's later texts, or to find the designers' reason for a rule, read `exploring.md`, "Weighing the sources".

## Changing the text: the revision form

Every change of the text has the four parts below, so that no disagreement between the text and an implementation stays hidden.

1. An entry in the revival section of Appendix I: a `\subsection` with a `\seclabel`. The entry gives:
   - the affected sections, the change, its rationale and its effect. The effect names each departure: each way in which walk or the compiled path does not do what the new text says, with its ledger row.
   - the original text, quoted with its path and line in `Specification-1.0-frozen/`;
   - what a reversal to the alternative not taken would need;
   - the decision of the curator that it follows (its POSITIONS entry), or the reason that your brief gives.

   For the form, print one entry, about 2 KB: `explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh 'doc:Specification/appendices/changes.tex#choice of a coercion'`.

2. At each changed passage, a callout that prints in every build, unlike a `\note`:

       \revision{<label>}{<what changed, in a sentence or two>}

   `<label>` is the `\seclabel` of the entry. `Specification/fortress/fortress.tex` defines `\revision`.

3. The front matter's one paragraph on the revision, in `Specification/fortress/preamble.tex`. If your change makes it false, correct it.

4. The full reasoning, in `decision-record.md` in the folder of your work under `explorations/`: each changed passage, the original and the new text, the reason, and the way back. For the form, print one passage of an earlier record, about 4 KB: `explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh 'doc:explorations/compile-ladder/rung-spec-route-a/decision-record.md#3.3'`.

If the revision refuses an example, keep the example in the text, marked "Not allowed", as the specification itself does. If your change contradicts a calculus of Appendix A, keep the calculus's rules and soundness claims. Add a callout to it that says what it predates.

Check each changed sentence of `Specification/` or `Documentation/` against the curator's decisions. If it says what walk or the compiled path does, run a program that shows it.

## Building it

To check your LaTeX, build the specification in a built tree, after the setup lines. It takes about 90 s, so start it detached (`session.md`, "Long commands"):

    nohup bash -c '( cd Specification/fortress && ./ant genSource && ./ant tex ) > tmp/spec.txt 2>&1; echo EXIT=$? >> tmp/spec.txt' >/dev/null 2>&1 &

- Both commands must end in `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, and `grep -c 'LaTeX Warning: Reference\|LaTeX Warning: Label .* multiply defined\|LaTeX Warning: There were multiply-defined labels\|^! Undefined control sequence' Specification/fortress/fortress.log` must print 0.
- If `pdflatex` is missing, install the packages of the `PKGS` line of `explorations/experiment/setup.sh` with `apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y`.
- The build writes only ignored files, its log among them, which can reach 400 MB. Remove them afterwards: `git clean -fXq -- Specification`.
- Update `Specification/fortress.pdf` only if your brief asks for it: copy `Specification/fortress/fortress.pdf` over it.

## When the text and an implementation disagree

- If a decision of the curator says which side is correct, the other side is wrong. If the wrong side is in your area, change it to agree. If not, record the departure as `tests-writing.md`, "How a defect is recorded", says.
- If no decision says so, the disagreement is a conflict. Switch to exploring (`exploring.md`).
- If the passage has an Appendix I entry, name the departure or the conflict in the entry's effect, with its ledger row. Then the text claims no more than holds.

## Citing it

- If your change renames or removes a section that a test names, update that citation in the same commit.
- Inside the text, cite a section with `\secref{label}`.

=== XXXGenericMethodBoundsDifferWalk.fss
(* Two generic dotted methods of one name and one number of parameters in an object, whose static parameters differ only in their bounds, are a valid overloading, and each call runs the most specific declaration whose bound holds its argument (overloading.tex, section "Declarations with Static Parameters"). *)
component XXXGenericMethodBoundsDifferWalk
export Executable

object Apart
    tk[\U extends Number\](y: U): ZZ32 = 2
    tk[\U extends String\](y: U): ZZ32 = 3
end

object Nested
    tk[\U extends Number\](y: U): ZZ32 = 2
    tk[\U extends ZZ32\](y: U): ZZ32 = 3
end

run(): () = do
    n: ZZ32 = 5
    m: ZZ64 = 6
    assert(Nested.tk(n), 3, "a ZZ32 takes the declaration bounded by ZZ32, the more specific")
    assert(Nested.tk(m), 2, "a ZZ64 takes the declaration bounded by Number")
    assert(Apart.tk(n), 2, "a ZZ32 takes the declaration bounded by Number")
    assert(Apart.tk("a"), 3, "a String takes the declaration bounded by String")
end

end
=== XXXAsIfGenericMethodOverloadsWalk.fss
(* Two generic dotted methods of one name that a trait declares, called on a receiver assumed at the trait, each run where the call's arguments fit it (type-annotation.tex, section "Type Assumption"). *)
component XXXAsIfGenericMethodOverloadsWalk
export Executable

trait Tk
    tk[\U\](y: U, z: U): U = z
    tk[\U\](y: U, z: U, w: U): U = w
end

object Inherits extends Tk end

run(): () = do
    assert((Inherits asif Tk).tk(1, 2), 2, "the trait's overload of two parameters")
    assert((Inherits asif Tk).tk(1, 2, 3), 3, "the trait's overload of three parameters")
end

end
=== XXXGenericPairTupleReturnWalk.fss
(* Two generic declarations, one inside the other, whose results are tuples holding each its own type parameter, are a valid overloading that loads, and each call runs the declaration that fits it. *)
component XXXGenericPairTupleReturnWalk
export Executable

trait Shape end
trait Round extends Shape end
object Circle extends Round end
object Square extends Shape end

ident[\T extends Shape\](x: T): (T, ZZ32) = (x, 1)
ident[\T extends Round\](x: T): (T, ZZ32) = (x, 2)

run(): () = do
    (a, i) = ident(Circle)
    (b, j) = ident(Square)
    assert(i, 2, "a Circle takes the declaration over Round")
    assert(j, 1, "a Square takes the declaration over Shape")
end

end
=== XXXGenericFunctionalMethodsExcludingWalk.fss
(* Two generic functional methods of one name and one number of parameters in an object, their parameter types excluding at a parameter without a static parameter, are a valid overloading, and each call runs the declaration that fits it. *)
component XXXGenericFunctionalMethodsExcludingWalk
export Executable

object O
    fm[\T\](self, x: T, z: ZZ32): ZZ32 = 1
    fm[\T\](self, x: T, z: String): ZZ32 = 2
end

run(): () = do
    assert(fm(O, 4, 5), 1, "the declaration over a ZZ32")
    assert(fm(O, 4, "a"), 2, "the declaration over a String")
end

end
=== XXXNumeralTypeReturnTypeWalk.fss
(* A numeral type is written only as a parameter's type: one written as a function's return type is refused at load, whether or not a numeral meets it. *)
component XXXNumeralTypeReturnTypeWalk
export Executable

never(x: ZZ32): NaturalNumeral[\1, 10, 3\] = never(x)

run(): () = do
    println("REACHED: a numeral type is a return type")
  end

end
=== GenericOverloadStaticArgKindsWalk.fss
(* Overloaded generic functions whose static parameters differ in kind, a nat parameter beside a type parameter, each run where the static argument that a call writes fits its parameter's kind (overloading.tex, section "Applicability to Named Functional Calls"). *)
component GenericOverloadStaticArgKindsWalk
export Executable

kd[\nat n\](x: ZZ32): ZZ32 = n
kd[\T\](x: T, y: T): ZZ32 = 7

run(): () = do
    assert(kd(1, 2), 7, "the type parameter's declaration, its static argument inferred")
    assert(kd[\3\](1), 3, "a nat written takes the declaration of the nat parameter")
    assert(kd[\ZZ32\](1, 2), 7, "a type written takes the declaration of the type parameter")
end

end
